_comment: Sample [[DICE_TABLES]] payload for the dice oracle (contracts/DICE_ORACLE.md). Paste the JSON below (without this _comment) into the CONTENT of one World-level World Info entry whose COMMENT/title contains the literal token [[DICE_TABLES]]. Keep the entry ENABLED (disable:false) but INERT (no keys, not constant) so it never injects itself — the Scene Tracker's Dice tab reads it out of the raw world data. Tuned for a slice-of-life commune where a free-spirited NPC recounts past flings, conjures temporary men on demand, and where a random event can break into the scene. Schema 2: a procedure's `mode` is "recount" (past, default) or "event" (about to happen now) and picks the built-in default framing when you omit one; `turns` sets how many upcoming replies a roll stays armed for (payload default + per-procedure override; the Dice tab can override per roll). `framing` is the lead-in prepended to the rolled facts; put HOW to narrate them in your world's system prompt (it can refer to the <dice_oracle> block by name).
framing: Here is some information regarding this recounted encounter. Treat every detail as an established fact and narrate the memory in-character around them:

man_build: a broad, heavy-set giant who could pin her to a wall one-handed
wiry and restless, never still for a second
soft and round, all warmth and no edges
lean and wickedly tall, all elbows and knees
shaggy and bear-like, more beard than face
man_vibe: painfully earnest and a little clueless
smooth-talking and far too pleased with himself
a chaos gremlin who treated every rule as a dare
gentle and unbothered, went along with anything
intense, treated a picnic like a military operation
setting: the back of a rusted-out van
a lake nobody was supposed to swim in
antic: an ambitious DIY project that got wildly out of hand
a skinny-dip that an audience stumbled onto
a food fight that turned into something else
an attempt to be quiet that failed spectacularly
a prank that backfired on both of them
event_kind: a sudden summer downpour drives everyone under cover
an unexpected visitor rolls up the drive
the power cuts out across the whole commune
a heated argument erupts two rooms over
a stray animal wanders in and won't leave
someone discovers the harvest has gone bad

text.messy: a ridiculous mess — but a fond, funny memory

text.trivial: a small mess, cleaned up and forgotten
text.notable: something that took real effort to live down
text.legendary: a trace still talked about / visible to this day

text.vanished: he drifted off and she never saw him again
text.showed_up_here: he actually turned up at the commune later

procedures.label: Something happens now
procedures.framing: The following is breaking into the scene right now — not a memory. These dice results establish what happens; treat them as true and narrate it unfolding in the present, in-character:

text.trouble: it makes things harder and puts everyone on edge
text.mixed: it's disruptive but not all bad
text.welcome: it turns out to be a genuinely lucky break

steps.label: Who has to deal with it

outcomes.1-3: the player is pulled in directly
outcomes.4-6: someone already in the scene takes the lead

text.yes: it leaves something to sort out afterward
